title: Search should ignore letter case
body:
## Problem

The shopping list cannot find an item unless the search uses the same capitalization as its name.

## Reproduce

Start the baseline app and type `milk` into Search. The seeded `Milk` item disappears. Searching for `Milk` finds it.

## Expected behavior

Search matches names without regard to letter case. Leading and trailing whitespace in the query is ignored. Clearing search restores all items.

## Acceptance criteria

- `milk`, `MILK`, and ` Milk ` find the seeded Milk item.
- Nonmatching searches show the existing empty-search message.
- Filtering does not modify saved data or the whole-list counts.
- Add a passing regression for B01 and retain the other exercises.

title: Sort quantities numerically, not alphabetically
body:
## Problem

The Quantity: low to high option puts two-digit quantities before smaller single-digit quantities.

## Reproduce

Start the baseline app, select Quantity: low to high, and compare Apples (10), Eggs (12), Bread (2), and Bananas (3).

## Expected behavior

The quantities should be 1, 1, 2, 3, 10, 12, not 1, 1, 10, 12, 2, 3.

## Acceptance criteria

- Sort all allowed quantities numerically in ascending order.
- Equal quantities keep their original relative order.
- Changing sort does not rewrite the stored item order.
- Add a passing regression for B02 and retain the other exercises.

title: The left-to-pick-up count includes bought items
body:
## Problem

The large left-to-pick-up number includes items already marked as bought.

## Reproduce

The baseline has six items, including two already bought. The sidebar says six left to pick up instead of four. Tick Milk and the number still does not decrease.

## Expected behavior

The remaining count measures unbought items, not quantities or currently visible search results.

## Acceptance criteria

- The baseline shows four remaining items; buying Milk changes it to three.
- Unchecking Milk restores four; buying every item results in zero.
- Search does not change whole-list statistics.
- Add a passing regression for B03 and retain the other exercises.

title: Edit an item's name and quantity
body:
## User story

As a shopper, I want to correct a name or quantity without deleting and recreating an item.

## Scope

Add a small, keyboard-accessible inline editor, and extend the existing item API. Keep the single-list, local JSON-file design.

## Acceptance criteria

- Edit the name and quantity of an existing item, with Save and Cancel controls.
- Reuse the existing trimmed name (1-80 characters) and integer quantity (1-99) rules on the server and in the UI.
- Cancel leaves the item unchanged.
- Saving preserves its ID, bought status, and list position; edits survive a restart.
- Show validation and save failures without losing the original item.
- Add focused UI/model/API coverage and update the app guide. Do not fix unrelated baseline bugs.

title: Clear all bought items in one step
body:
## User story

As a shopper starting my next trip, I want to clear items already in the bag without deleting them one at a time.

## Scope

Add a Clear bought action with confirmation, backed by one server operation and one atomic file write.

## Acceptance criteria

- Show how many items will be removed and require confirmation.
- Cancel removes nothing; confirm removes only bought items.
- The action applies to the entire list, not just visible search results.
- Disable the action when there are no bought items.
- Repeating the API operation is safe; remaining items survive a restart.
- Add focused tests and update the app guide. Do not fix unrelated baseline bugs.

title: Download the list as a plain-text checklist
body:
## User story

As a shopper, I want a simple downloadable checklist that I can open or print without this app.

## Scope

Add a Download list button and a backend endpoint returning UTF-8 plain text. No extra packages, accounts, or external services.

## Acceptance criteria

- Download `shopping-list.txt` containing the entire list in saved order, regardless of the current search or sort.
- Include one line per item, for example `[ ] Milk x 1` or `[x] Bread x 2`.
- Preserve Unicode names without treating names as HTML or executable content.
- An empty list produces a useful plain-text message.
- Export never changes saved data. Add endpoint tests and update the app guide.
